newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak blue chips gain as SAX index at yr-high.
newsitem.headline: Slovak blue chips gain as SAX index at yr-high.

text.p: Slovak blue chips closed mostly higher in livelier trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Friday, pushing the SAX index up 3.44 points to a year-high of 205.16.
Oil and gas storage company Nafta led net advancers, closing up 94 crowns at 1,695, but brokers noted that only one Nafta share was traded during the session.
Steel producer VSZ matched 5,785 shares on the floor to close up four crowns at 710.
"We think VZS shares have become overheated, rising too much and too quickly, and so we see it retreating slightly in the near future," said Dusan Sykora of ING Barings.
Sykora added that the expected decline should not be too dramatic and the share's development would be in line with the cyclical trend common for blue chips on the Slovak market.
Oil refiner Slovnaft rose 29 crowns to reach its nominal value of 1,000 crowns, and dealers predicted the issue to increase further, boosted by the current strong demand.
"Slovnaft's share should drive the entire bourse higher in coming days, so we can say that the market will extend its gains over the mid-term," Sykora said.
Overall volume rose to 515,710 shares, boosted mainly by direct trades, from 380,897 stocks traded on Thursday while turnover increased to 670.11 million crowns, from 527.97 million on Thursday.
